The Prophet told Abu Dharr that under rulers who delay prayer beyond its time he should pray at its proper time and count praying with them as voluntary.
Prayer in congregation is twenty-five or twenty-seven degrees more excellent than prayer said alone.
The Prophet said he had thought of burning the houses of men absent from congregational and Friday prayers, and that the night and morning prayers weigh most on hypocrites.
A blind man hearing the call was told to answer it; Ibn Mas'ud said only known hypocrites or the sick stayed away; one leaving after the call disobeyed the Prophet.
Praying Isha in congregation is like praying half the night and the morning prayer like praying all night; whoever prays the morning prayer is under Allah's protection.
The Prophet prayed in blind Itban's house to mark a prayer place for him, and there said Allah forbids the Fire to whoever declares His oneness seeking His pleasure.
The Prophet led Anas and his household in prayer at home, Anas standing behind him with an orphan or alone at his right, and the women behind them.
The Prophet prayed and prostrated on a small mat, his garment touching Maimuna beside him when he prostrated.
Congregational prayer exceeds praying at home or market by over twenty degrees; each step to the mosque raises a degree, and angels pray for those waiting there in ablution.
Walking far to prayer brings greater reward; the Prophet told a distant Ansari and Banu Salama their steps were recorded, each erasing a sin or raising a degree.
The five daily prayers wipe away sins just as bathing five times a day in a river at one's door would leave no dirt.
Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or evening, Allah prepares a feast for him in Paradise each morning or evening.
After the dawn prayer the Prophet sat in his place until the sun had risen, while his companions talked of the days of ignorance and laughed and he only smiled.
The places dearest to Allah are the mosques and the most hateful to Him are the markets.
The one best versed in the Quran leads the prayer, then the most knowing of the Sunnah, earliest emigrant or eldest; the Prophet told young visitors their oldest should lead.
After bowing in prayer the Prophet asked Allah to rescue helpless Muslims, send famine on Mudar and curse other tribes, stopping once they were rescued or a verse came.
For a month in the dawn prayer, after bowing, the Prophet cursed Ri'l, Dhakwan, Lihyan and Usayya, who killed the seventy reciters at Bi'r Ma'una, and then abandoned it.
The Prophet recited Qunut in the dawn and evening prayers, and in prayer cursed Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and Usayya, saying Allah pardoned Ghifar and protected Aslam.
On journeys the Prophet and his companions slept past sunrise, moved on, then prayed the dawn prayer; he said sleep is no fault, and a little water sufficed everyone.
Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it should pray it when he remembers, its only expiation, for Allah said to observe prayer for His remembrance.
Prayer was prescribed as two rak'ahs and kept so on journeys; shortening is Allah's charity, and the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman prayed only two rak'ahs travelling.
The Prophet shortened to two rak'ahs at Dhu'l-Hulaifa and after three miles or farsakhs, and kept praying two rak'ahs during a ten-day stay in Mecca until returning to Medina.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar prayed two rak'ahs at Mina, as did Uthman at first before praying four, which Ibn Mas'ud regretted; Ibn Umar prayed four behind the imam.
On cold, windy or rainy nights the Prophet had the caller tell people to pray in their dwellings, as Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas did, even on a rainy Friday.
On journeys the Prophet prayed voluntary prayers and witr on his mount facing wherever it went, but not obligatory ones; the verse on Allah's face wherever you turn concerns this.
When hurrying on a journey the Prophet combined sunset with Isha and noon with afternoon, delaying the first prayer to the time of the second.
The Prophet combined noon with afternoon and sunset with Isha in Medina without fear, rain or journey, and on the Tabuk expedition, so his Ummah would not face hardship.
After prayer the Prophet turned to the left as well as to the right, and companions liked to stand at his right so his face would turn to them.
Once the iqama is given only the obligatory prayer is prayed; the Prophet questioned men who prayed alone after the dawn prayer had begun.
Entering the mosque one asks Allah to open the doors of His mercy and prays two rak'ahs before sitting, as the Prophet told Jabir and did after journeys.
Aisha said the Prophet prayed the forenoon prayer only after journeys, or prayed four rak'ahs or more; Umm Hani saw him pray eight rak'ahs when Mecca was conquered.
Charity is due on every bone each morning and two forenoon rak'ahs suffice; Abu Huraira and Abu Darda were told to fast three days monthly, pray forenoon and witr.
The Prophet prayed two short rak'ahs between the call and iqama of the dawn prayer, kept them more than any voluntary prayer, and said they are better than the world.
In the two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer the Prophet recited 'Say: O unbelievers' and 'Say: Allah is One', or verses from al-Baqara and Al Imran.
Allah builds a house in Paradise for whoever prays twelve voluntary rak'ahs a day, and Ibn Umar listed those he prayed with the Prophet before and after the obligatory prayers.
Aisha described the Prophet's long night prayer standing or sitting, bowing from the position he recited in, and in old age reciting seated but standing to recite before bowing.
In his last year or two the Prophet prayed most voluntary prayers sitting; he said a seated prayer is worth half, but he is not like others.
Aisha said the Prophet prayed eleven or thirteen rak'ahs at night with witr, in Ramadan or not, then two short rak'ahs before dawn, and that his heart did not sleep.
The Prophet slept early and rose late in the night or at cockcrow to pray, loved regular deeds, and after the two dawn rak'ahs talked with Aisha or lay down.
The Prophet prayed witr every night, early, at midnight or late, finishing it by dawn, and woke Aisha to pray her witr.
